title: Effect of Ca addition on grain refinement of Mg-9Li-1Al alloy

nodes.label: Duplex Mg-Li alloys solidify with very coarse lamellar alpha-Mg and coarse beta-Li grains, which limits their usable properties
A small Ca addition should form Al2Ca particles that nucleate both alpha-Mg and beta-Li heterogeneously and refine the structure
Mg-9Li-1Al (LA91) duplex alpha+beta alloy as the base
Add 0.2 wt% Ca so that the alloy's own Al is consumed as Al2Ca
LA91 against LA91-0.2Ca, each examined as-cast and after identical extrusion
Melt in a vacuum induction furnace under argon at 720 C and cast
Hot extrude the cast billets at 250 C with an extrusion ratio of 28.2
Al2Ca forms in the Ca-bearing alloy alongside alpha-Mg and beta-Li and is absent from LA91
Sub-micron to ~1 um Al2Ca particles lie along the alpha/beta phase boundaries and inside both matrices, before and after extrusion
With Ca the as-cast alpha-Mg changes from long interconnected lamellar rods to isolated granular blocks
Ca refines both phases: as-cast alpha-Mg to ~28 um and as-extruded beta-Li from 10.32 to 4.56 um
Non-deforming Al2Ca particles act as heterogeneous nuclei for alpha-Mg on solidification and as dynamic-recrystallisation nucleation sites for beta-Li during extrusion
Al2Ca and beta-Li share the only plane pair below the 6% critical misfit, {311}Al2Ca/{110}beta-Li, with parallel close-packed directions
The refined duplex structure is expected to raise yield strength through the Hall-Petch relation
0.2 wt% Ca forms crystallographically potent Al2Ca that refines both alpha-Mg and beta-Li in Mg-9Li-1Al, cast and extruded
The etchant reveals only phase boundaries, so beta-Li refinement cannot be judged in the as-cast alloy
The quoted 1371.56 um alpha-Mg rod length is longer than the field of view of the micrograph it is credited to
Light alpha-Mg goes from long interconnected lamellae in LA91 to isolated blocky grains in LA91-0.2Ca on the dark beta-Li background

nodes.label: Of the close-packed plane pairs only {311}Al2Ca/{110}beta-Li has an interplanar misfit below the 6% critical value
Edge-to-edge matching model: a nucleant is potent when matching close-packed planes differ by under 6% and matching directions by under 10%
beta-Li is bcc with a = 0.351 nm and Al2Ca has a = 0.804 nm, with three near close-packed planes each
Mg-40Sr and Mg-30Y master alloys refine the beta-Li phase of Mg-14Li
Hall-Petch: a smaller grain size raises yield strength by adding boundary area that impedes dislocation motion
From the Mg-Al ternary diagram the solubility of Al in Mg on solidification exceeds the 1 wt% Al of LA91

notes: Structure-only paper: no property is measured, so the spine runs HYP -> DES -> PRC -> STR -> MEC -> PRP(basis=argued, Hall-Petch) -> DSC. Two branches meet at the refinement claim g11: solidification refinement of alpha-Mg (g6 -> g8/g9 -> g12 -> g10) and extrusion refinement of beta-Li (g7 -> g11). The crystallographic branch (g13, p10, p11, q1, q2) is what makes the nucleation claim more than an attribution. Numbers come from the panels: ~20-50 um granular alpha-Mg against the 100 um bar of F1b, ~10 um vs 4-5 um beta grains against the 25 um bars of F3a/F3b. Audit g17: F1a is about 450 um across at its 100 um bar, so the 1371.56 um rod length and 322.61 um width the text credits to it cannot be read there. Audit g16 is the paper's own (the etchant shows only phase boundaries). Panel-section defects: the 'definition' caption spans are offset and garbled, F2a and F4a both carry 'at now resolution dotted line area, and EDS analysis of' (the caption itself reads 'now' for 'low'), and F4b shows no A or B markers although the caption places both EDS points there. Lost: the full list of misfit values and matching directions, the Al2Ca/alpha-Mg matching pairs, and the F5 atom-configuration drawing (carried as text_only p11).

changes: p3: image_note corrected after the judge opened and enlarged F1d. The Al2Ca markers are an arrowed weak peak near 31.5 deg, the strong 37 deg peak and an arrowed weak peak near 79-81 deg; the 48 deg reflection carries an alpha-Mg triangle, not a diamond. The node's claim, its panel ids and its partial image_support stand.

panel_checks.note: F1c's legend is alpha-Mg and beta-Li only; F1d adds the Al2Ca diamond. The claim that Al2Ca reflections appear only in the Ca-bearing pattern is shown. The two patterns also differ strongly in relative peak heights (37 deg tallest in F1c, 32 deg in F1d), as the note says.

Same 25 um bar in both. F3a's beta grains run ~10-15 um with a clearly resolved boundary network; F3b's network is much denser at ~4-5 um, and the alpha-Mg bands are more numerous and more strongly curved, as the node's image_note states.

F4b shows one ~3 um agglomerate of bright particles in the centre plus sub-micron particles on the boundaries, and carries no A or B markers although the caption places the EDS points in it. The node's reading of an agglomerate rather than a dispersion is right, and partial is the correct image_support.

review.audit_summary: Two audit nodes, under budget, both genuine and both stated as limits rather than contradictions: g16 (the etchant reveals only phase boundaries, so as-cast beta-Li refinement cannot be judged) and g17 with p2 (the quoted 1371.56 um alpha-Mg rod length exceeds the ~450 um field of F1a). Both bound the refinement claim g11, which is the paper's headline. The graph handles the no-property case correctly: the single PRP node g14 carries basis=argued for the Hall-Petch expectation, so nothing unmeasured is passed off as evidenced. Spine is 15 nodes on one path with the crystallographic branch (g13, p10, p11) feeding the nucleation mechanism g12. No invented panel ids.
